messages.subject: A Few Questions from a Newbie about Getting Started with devtools
messages.subject_clean: A Few Questions from a Newbie about Getting Started with devtools
messages.body_plain: I consider myself a novice to intermediate R programmer and have a few good ideas for libraries that I would move forward with. I am a newbie in terms of developing libraries and I have no experience building R libraries but would like to get that understanding. I have pretty much no experience with GitHub but I do have an account. I have devtools installed. My first question is, how to initialize a new project and can devtools automatically create a GitHub repository under my user name and install the correct directory structure there. I am guessing that this is the case because of the install_github() command in devtools although I'm not sure. Can somebody provide with some clear insight how to "sync my application from my computer with my GitHub repository", also can somebody please explain the idea of pull request?

messages.subject: Re: A Few Questions from a Newbie about Getting Started with devtools
messages.subject_clean: A Few Questions from a Newbie about Getting Started with devtools
messages.body_plain:
Congratulations on taking the next step, and good look with your package ideas.  If you're going to learn package development, I recommend reading Hadley's  R Packages <http://shop.oreilly.com/product/0636920034421.do> book.  Not only will it answer most developer's existing and upcoming questions, it will reframe the situation and make their approach more coherent/consistent.  But here are pointers for your specific questions.  They're great questions for someone at this stage, and fortunately a lot of good stuff exists to answer them.

> how to initialize a new project and can devtools automatically create a GitHub repository under my user name and install the correct directory structure there.

 The best place to start is probably the package chapter <http://r-pkgs.had.co.nz/package.html> and the GitHub chapter <http://r-pkgs.had.co.nz/git.html>.

> I am guessing that this is the case because of the install_github() command in devtools although I'm not sure.

This function is actually for installing other people's packages <http://www.inside-r.org/packages/cran/devtools/docs/install_github> that are hosted on GitHub.  Its primary purpose is not for developing your own package.

> Can somebody provide with some clear insight how to "sync my application from my computer with my GitHub repository", also can somebody please explain the idea of pull request?

Within the world of R packages, see the "Making a pull request" section, toward the end of the GitHub chapter <http://r-pkgs.had.co.nz/git.html>.  One of the successful strategies of RStudio developers is that they build on existing frameworks and approaches; one advantage is that you can exploit that much larger non-R world's knowledge.  For example, in the GitHub Guides <https://guides.github.com/>, I recommend starting with Getting your project on GitHub <https://guides.github.com/introduction/getting-your-project-on-github/> and Understanding the GitHub Flow <https://guides.github.com/introduction/flow/>.

messages.subject: devtools build not filling man or R directories
messages.subject_clean: devtools build not filling man or R directories
messages.body_plain:
Hello

I believe I've been following the given directions but I can not seem to create a package using devtools so I think I'm missing a critical step.  I'm using the latest versions of R and relevant packages.  I'm using a MacBook Pro (updated OSX10.11.2).

I begin with a directory (DevTTools) that has single file in it that contains two simple functions (mymin and mymax, simple calls to min and max functions).  Preceding both of these functions is the code to build the documentation.

At this point I setwd to the parent (DevTTools) and run build().   It seems to run correctly -- I'm not sure exactly what the output should be but I can see that the DESCRIPTION and NAMESPACE files are created as well as the R and man directories.  However, there's nothing in the R and man directories and the tar.gz file that is created also does not have anything in the R or man directories.   What am I missing?

In some of the devtools instructions, one is told to download Xcode.  I've done that but don't know how to use it, the instructions make little or no mention of what to do with it, and I am not seeing the connection between Xcode and devtools.  I'm thinking this might be part of my problem but I haven't found any instruction on this.

R Code for my test file:
#' My minimum
#'
#' Finds the minimum value within a vector of values in \code{\link{mymin}}
#'
#' @param vlist a vector of numbers
#'
#' @return a real number
#'
#' @examples
#' mymin(c(1,2,3,4,5))
#'
#' @export
#' mymin()
mymin <- function(vlist){
d <- min(vlist)
return(d)
}
#' My maximum
#'
#' Finds the maximum value within a vector of values in \code{\link{mymax}}
#'
#' @param vlist a vector of numbers
#'
#' @return a real number
#'
#' @examples
#' mymax(c(1,2,3,4,5))
#'
#' @export
#' mymax()
mymax <- function(vlist){
d <- max(vlist)
return(d)
}
